'''Michael Alexander Conley Jr. ''' (born October 11, 1987) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was drafted as the fourth overall pick in the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].

Mike Conley Jr. played basketball for [[Lawrence North High School]] in Indianapolis. Conley played alongside [[Greg Oden]], a future Ohio State teammate and NBA first-overall draft pick. The duo won three state championships and 103 games during their four years at high school. Conley spent 12 seasons with the Grizzlies and became the team's all-time leading scorer before being traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in 2019, where he would make his first All-Star Game in 2021, before being traded again to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in 2023, where he played for three seasons. Conley has the most [[NBA Sportsmanship Award]]s of all time, with four selections. On July 7, 2026, Conley signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].

==College career==
In his freshman year at Ohio State, Conley averaged 11.3 points and led the [[Big Ten Conference]] in [[Assist (basketball)|assists]] with 6.1 per game. Conley and fellow freshman star [[Greg Oden]] led the [[Ohio State Buckeyes|Buckeyes]] to a Big Ten conference championship and a runner-up finish in the [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/mike_conley/bio/ Mike Conley Stats, Video, Bio, Profile]</ref>

On the road to the championship game, the Buckeyes defeated [[Central Connecticut State Blue Devils men's basketball|Central Connecticut State]], [[Xavier University (Cincinnati)|Xavier]], [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], and [[Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball|Georgetown]]. They lost the championship game to the repeat national champion [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. Conley's best performance in the tournament was in the game against Xavier. He recorded 21 points, 4 assists, 2 steals, and 3 blocks as Ohio State defeated the Musketeers in [[Overtime (sports)|overtime]]. Oden fouled out in regulation, and Conley scored 11 of his 21 points in the extra period.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=274000034 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180621065957/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=274000034 |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 21, 2018 |title=Xavier vs. Ohio State - Game Recap - March 17, 2007 - ESPN |website=ESPN.com |language=en |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref>

Ending the season with totals of 441 points and 238 assists, Conley was named to the All-Big Ten First Team.

After his freshman year, Conley announced his intention to enter the [[2007 NBA draft]], as did Oden. To preserve his eligibility to withdraw from the draft, he initially did not sign with an agent, but he signed with his father several weeks before the draft.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2007/news/story?id=2843539 |title=Source: Oden ends speculation, to declare for NBA |date=2007-04-20 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Memphis Grizzlies (2007–2019)===

====2007–2010: early years====
Conley joined fellow Buckeyes [[Greg Oden]] and [[Daequan Cook]] in declaring for the [[2007 NBA draft]]; both Conley and Oden were represented by Conley's father, whom the NBA certified as an agent earlier in the year. The [[Memphis Grizzlies]] drafted Conley as the fourth overall pick after Oden, [[Kevin Durant]], and [[Al Horford]].

Conley had his first major appearances in January 2008. In his first five career games, he scored 5, 10, 11, 11, and 15 points, respectively. He scored a season-high 20 points with 7 assists in a 134–124 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/conlemi01/gamelog/2008/ |title=Mike Conley 2007-08 Game Log |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref> Conley finished his rookie year with averages of 9.4 points and 4.2 assists per game.

Conley started his sophomore campaign competing with [[Kyle Lowry]] for minutes. On January 25, 2009, the Grizzlies made [[Lionel Hollins]] the head coach after [[Marc Iavaroni]] was fired. On February 19, 2009, Lowry was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]], which put Conley in the starting lineup. He averaged 10.8 points and 4.3 assists per game for the year.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Mike Conley Career Stats - NBA |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/3195/mike-conley-jr |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

Conley cemented his role as a full-time starter for the Grizzlies in 2009. He posted a season high of 25 points on March 31, 2010, during a 106–102 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/conlemi01/gamelog/2010/ |title=Mike Conley 2009-10 Game Log |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref> He averaged 12.0 points and 5.3 assists on the season.<ref name=":0" />

====2010–2014: All-Defensive Team selection and Conference finals====
On November 30, 2010, Conley put up a season-high 28 points in a 98–96 victory over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He averaged 13.7 and 6.5 assists on the year to help the Grizzlies make the playoffs for the first time in five years. Entering with the eighth seed in the Western Conference, they defeated the top-seeded [[San Antonio Spurs]] in six games in the first round, making NBA history as only the second eighth-seeded team to defeat a first seed in a seven-game series. They then lost to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in seven games in the semifinals.

In the shortened [[2011 NBA lockout|lockout season]], Conley played 62 of the Grizzlies' 66 games, during which he averaged 12.7 points and 6.5 assists. The Grizzlies made the playoffs but fell in the first round to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] in seven games.

That year, Conley averaged 14.6 points, 6.1 assists, and 2.8 rebounds per game as the Grizzlies made the playoffs once again. They eliminated the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] and the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] to reach the Western Conference Finals for the first time in franchise history. They then lost to the [[San Antonio Spurs]] in four games. Conley was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] for the first time.[[File:Mike Conley driving past Chris Paul 20131118 Clippers v Grizzles.jpg|250px|thumb|right|Conley driving past [[Chris Paul]] in a game in November 2013]]
Conley averaged a career-high 17.2 points, 6.0 assists, and 2.9 rebounds per game on the year as the Grizzles made the playoffs for the fourth consecutive season. They were eliminated in the first round by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a seven-game series. Conley received the [[NBA Sportsmanship Award]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mike Conley wins Dumars Trophy|website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|date=April 24, 2014|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/10832242/mike-conley-memphis-grizzlies-wins-nba-sportsmanship-award|access-date=May 11, 2020}}</ref>

====2014–2019: playoff disappointment====
On December 13, 2014, Conley scored a career-high 36 points to help the Grizzlies defeat the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], 120–115, in overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.nj.com/sixers/2014/12/conleys_36_lead_grizzlies_past.html |title=Conley's 36 lead Grizzlies past 76ers in overtime, 120-115 |date=2014-12-14 |website=nj.com |language=en-US |access-date=2019-07-31}}</ref> The Grizzlies finished the season as the fifth seed in the Western Conference, making the playoffs once again. They defeated the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in the first round in five games. Near the end of game 3, Conley suffered a facial fracture, which forced him to miss the rest of the first round. He also missed game 1 of the semifinals against the [[Golden State Warriors]]. Conley returned in game 2 of the series and, while wearing a protective mask, scored 21 points to lead Memphis to a victory. Memphis eventually lost to the Warriors in six games.<ref>[https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/conlemi01/gamelog/2015/ Mike Conley 2014–15 Game Log]</ref>

In 2014, Conley received what would have been the first [[technical foul]] of his NBA career, but it was overturned by league officials the next day; as of May 2025 he has yet to record a technical in over 34,000 minutes played, having by far the longest streak without one of any NBA player.<ref name="techperf">{{Cite web |url=https://www.wsj.com/amp/articles/mike-conley-the-nba-player-who-is-technically-perfect-1492090233 |title=The NBA Player Who Is Technically Perfect |last=Cohen |first=Ben |date=April 13, 2017 |work=[[Wall Street Journal]]}}</ref>

On October 31, 2015, Conley surpassed [[Shareef Abdur-Rahim]] (7,801) for third on the Grizzlies' career scoring list. He scored 22 points against the Brooklyn Nets to finish the game with 7,821 career points.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20151031/BKNMEM/gameinfo.html Conley scores 22 points as Grizzlies defeat Nets 101–91]</ref> On January 18, 2016, Conley returned to the lineup after missing six games with a sore left Achilles and recorded his third double-double of the season with 15 points and 10 assists, helping the Grizzlies defeat the New Orleans Pelicans 101–99. Earlier that day, he was named one of the 30 finalists for the 2016 U.S. Olympic team.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20160118/NOPMEM/gameinfo.html Gasol helps Memphis beat New Orleans 101–99]</ref> On March 12, he was ruled out for three to four weeks with a left foot injury.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/conley-anderson-update-160312 Mike Conley & Chris Anderson Update]</ref> He was later ruled out for the rest of the season on April 4 after a reevaluation by team doctors, and hoped to return for the playoffs.<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/15136263/mike-conley-memphis-grizzlies-likely-done-season Sources: Mike Conley (Achilles) unlikely to return to Grizzlies lineup]</ref> The injury-riddled Grizzlies finished seventh in the Western Conference, and without Conley and [[Marc Gasol]], were swept by the San Antonio Spurs in the first round of the playoffs. On April 23, Conley received the NBA Sportsmanship Award for the second time.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/conley-sportsmanship-award-160423|title=Mike Conley awarded 2015-16 NBA's Sportsmanship Award|work=NBA.com|date=April 23, 2016|access-date=April 27, 2016}}</ref>

On July 14, 2016, Conley re-signed with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/conley-singed-160714|title=Grizzlies re-sign Mike Conley to multi-year contract|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 14, 2016}}</ref> His reported five-year, $153 million deal was the greatest contract by total value in NBA history at the time.<ref>{{cite web|last=Stein|first=Marc|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/16684308/mike-conley-memphis-grizzlies-agree-principle-5-year-153-million-deal|title=Sources: Mike Conley, Grizzlies agree in principle on 5-year, $153 million deal|work=ESPN.com|date=July 2, 2016|access-date=July 14, 2016}}</ref> On November 16, 2016, he scored 30 points and hit a career-high-tying seven three-pointers in a 111–107 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899617|title=Grizzlies beat Clippers 111-107 on Gasol's late 3-pointer|work=ESPN.com|date=November 16, 2016|access-date=November 17, 2016}}</ref> On November 29, he was ruled out for six to eight weeks with a fractured vertebra.<ref>{{cite web|last=Wojnarowski|first=Adrian|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources-mike-conley-has-fracture-in-his-vertebrae-190316157.html|title=Sources: Mike Conley out 6 to 8 weeks with fractured vertebrae|work=Yahoo.com|date=November 29, 2016|access-date=November 29, 2016}}</ref> He returned to action on December 16 after missing nine games. In the Grizzlies' 96–92 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]], Conley passed [[Pau Gasol]] to become the all-time leading scorer in Grizzlies history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899836|title=Cousins, Koufos lead Kings to 96-92 win over Grizzlies|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2016|access-date=December 17, 2016}}</ref> On January 30, 2017, he scored 38 points in a 115–98 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. Conley matched his career best with seven three-pointers (in 10 attempts) and made 12 of 18 shots overall in his fourth 30-point game of the season—he previously had five over his entire career.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900144|title=Conley scores career-high 38, Grizzlies rout Suns 115-96|work=ESPN.com|date=January 30, 2017|access-date=January 31, 2017}}</ref> On February 15 against New Orleans, Conley passed [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1980)|Mike Miller]] for the most three-pointers in franchise history with 845.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900246 | title=Hill's 23 points, 18 from Davis lead Pelicans past Grizzlies | work=ESPN.com | date=February 15, 2017 | access-date=February 16, 2017}}</ref> On March 29, he matched his career-high with seven three-pointers on his way to 36 points, helping the Grizzlies rout the [[Indiana Pacers]], 110–97.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900511|title=Conley scores 36 as Grizzlies rout Pacers 110-97|work=ESPN.com|date=March 29, 2017|access-date=March 30, 2017}}</ref>

On April 22, 2017, Conley scored a franchise postseason record 35 points in a 110–108 overtime win over the Spurs. The win tied the first-round series at 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400950397|title=Tied at 2: Gasol lifts Grizzlies past Spurs 110-108 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=April 22, 2017|access-date=April 23, 2017}}</ref>

Conley appeared in 12 of the Grizzlies' first 13 games of the 2017–18 season before suffering a left Achilles injury.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/conlemi01/gamelog/2018/|title=Mike Conley 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=January 27, 2018}}</ref> On January 27, 2018, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after requiring surgery to smooth a small bone protrusion in his left heel.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/medical-updates-180127|title=Grizzlies announce medical update for Conley, Parsons, Green and Ennis|work=NBA.com|date=January 27, 2018|access-date=January 27, 2018}}</ref>

In the Grizzlies' season opener on October 17, 2018, Conley made his first regular season appearance since November 2017 after missing 70 games. He played nearly 29 minutes, scored 11 points, and had three assists and one steal in a 111–83 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070695|title=Bogdanovic scores 19 points, Pacers rout Grizzlies 111-83|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}}</ref> On November 2, he scored a season-high 28 points in a 110–100 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070803|title=Conley, Gasol help Grizzlies top short-handed Jazz 110-100|work=ESPN.com|date=November 2, 2018|access-date=November 2, 2018}}</ref> On November 10, he set a new season high with 32 points in a 112–106 overtime win over the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070860|title=Conley scored 32 points sending Grizzles past 76ers in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2018|access-date=November 11, 2018}}</ref> On November 30, Conley improved his season-high scoring to 37 points and also made 10 assists in a 131–125 double-overtime win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Conley carries Grizzlies past Nets 131-125 in 2OTs |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071004 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=February 20, 2019 |date=November 30, 2018}}</ref> On March 5, 2019, he scored a career-high 40 points in a Grizzlies' 120–111 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. He was scoreless in the first quarter and scored 19 points in the fourth.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071635|title=Conley's career-high sends Grizzlies past Portland 120-111|work=ESPN.com|date=March 5, 2019|access-date=March 5, 2019}}</ref> On March 11, he was named Western Conference Player of the Week for games played from March 4 to March 10. It marked his first career Player of the Week award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/mike-conley-named-nba-western-conference-player-of-the-week-190311|title=Mike Conley named NBA Western Conference Player of the Week|work=NBA.com|date=March 11, 2019|access-date=March 12, 2019}}</ref> On March 27, in a 118–103 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]], Conley passed Marc Gasol to become the Grizzlies' all-time leader in career points.<ref>{{cite web |title=Curry, Durant each score 28 points, Warriors beat Grizzlies |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071791 |website=ESPN.com |access-date=March 28, 2019 |date=March 27, 2019 |quote=Grizzlies: Conley's 3-pointer with 2:50 left in the second quarter moved him to first place on the franchise scoring list, passing former teammate Marc Gasol.}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2019–2023)===

====2019–2021: first All-Star selection====
On July 6, 2019, Conley was traded to the [[Utah Jazz]] in exchange for [[Grayson Allen]], [[Jae Crowder]], [[Kyle Korver]], the draft rights to [[Darius Bazley]], and a protected first-round pick.<ref>{{cite web |title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Grayson Allen, Jae Crowder, Kyle Korver, draft rights to Darius Bazley and future first round draft pick from Utah Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-utah-jazz-trade-190706 |website=Memphis Grizzlies |publisher=NBA |access-date=July 6, 2019 |language=en |date=July 6, 2019}}</ref> He made his Jazz debut on October 23, recording five points and five assists in a 100–95 win over the Thunder.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MITCHELL HAS 32 AND 12, LEADS JAZZ OVER THUNDER 100-95 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900011 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On October 30, he scored a season-high 29 points, alongside five assists and two steals, in a 110–96 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=CONLEY BREAKS OUT, JAZZ BEAT CLIPPERS AS LEONARD RESTS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900063 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> In 2020, due to the suspension of the NBA season because of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the NBA produced a televised event in which NBA and [[WNBA]] players participated in a virtual H–O–R–S–E competition while quarantining at their respective homes. The NBA raised $200,000 for charities as Conley won the first virtual [[NBA All-Star Weekend H–O–R–S–E Competition|NBA H–O–R–S–E Competition]], becoming the inaugural "H.O.R.S.E Champion".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Mike Conley beats Chicago's Zach LaVine to win ESPN's HORSE competition |website=[[NBA.com]] |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/mike-conley-beats-chicagos-zach-lavine-win-espns-horse-competition}}</ref>

On August 21, 2020, during the first round of the playoffs, Conley recorded 27 points and a playoff career-high seven 3-pointers in a 124–87 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]] in Game 3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=BACK FROM QUARANTINE, CONLEY LEADS JAZZ OVER NUGGETS 124-87 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0041900163 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He had missed the first two games of the series after being quarantined. Two days later, Conley logged 26 points, four assists and two steals in a 129–127 win in Game 4. Despite taking a 3–1 series lead, the Jazz lost in seven games to the Nuggets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NUGGETS EDGE JAZZ 80-78 TO COMPLETE COMEBACK FROM 3-1 DOWN |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0041900167 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> After the 2019–20 season, Conley declined to exercise the early termination option on his contract, and was owed $34.5 million in the fifth and final year of his contract in 2020–21.<ref>{{cite news|first=Eric|last=Walden|title=Mike Conley declines early termination option, will return to Utah Jazz|date=November 12, 2020|newspaper=The Salt Lake Tribune|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/jazz/2020/11/12/mike-conley-declines/|access-date=November 24, 2020}}</ref>

On January 1, 2021, Conley scored a season-high 33 points and added seven assists, two rebounds, and one steal in a 106–100 win over the Clippers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/mike-conley-ties-career-high-seven-3-pointers-utah-jazzs-win-over-la-clipperrs|title=Mike Conley ties career-high with seven 3-pointers in Utah Jazz's win over L.A. Clippers|website=NBA.com|date=January 1, 2021|access-date=January 1, 2021}}</ref> He was named an [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] for the first time in his career as it was announced that he would be a reserve for the [[2021 NBA All-Star Game]], replacing the injured [[Devin Booker]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/03/06/jazz-guard-mike-conley-jr-added-nba-all-star-game-roster|title=Report: Mike Conley Added to All-Star Game Roster}}</ref> His 14-year wait is the longest ever for a first time All-Star.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mike Conley's All-Star wait is finally coming to an end|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/mike-conleys-all-star-wait-finally-coming-end|access-date=2021-03-22|website=Utah Jazz|language=en}}</ref> He recorded three points, one rebound, and two assists in 12 minutes in the game.<ref>{{Cite web|title=LBN vs DRT Mar 7, 2021 {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/game/lbn-vs-drt-0032000001/box-score#box-score|access-date=2021-03-22|website=www.nba.com}}</ref> Conley was also announced as Booker's replacement in the [[Three-Point Contest]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2934747-jazz-pg-mike-conley-reportedly-invited-to-2021-nba-all-star-game|title=Mike Conley Named Devin Booker's Injury Replacement for 2021 NBA All-Star Game|website=[[Bleacher Report]]}}</ref> where he competed against teammate [[Donovan Mitchell]]. Conley lost in the final round to [[Stephen Curry]], 28–27.<ref>{{cite news|first=Eva|last=Wallace|title=Nets steal some All-Star Game shine with reported Blake Griffin deal|date=March 7, 2021|newspaper=The Washington Post|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/03/07/nba-all-star-game-dunk-contest/#link-7OIEPFPBV5BA5FRMQPAMT2WTCQ|access-date=March 8, 2021}}</ref>

On May 29, during the first round of the playoffs, Conley scored 27 points and matched his playoff career-high of seven 3-pointers in a 121–111 win over the Grizzlies in game 3.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MITCHELL SCORES 29 POINTS, JAZZ BEAT GRIZZLIES FOR 2-1 LEAD |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000143 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> He missed the first five games of the Jazz's second-round series versus the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] due to a strained right hamstring.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz guard Mike Conley out for Game 5 vs. LA Clippers |url=https://www.deseret.com/2021/6/16/22537040/utah-jazz-guard-mike-conley-out-for-game-5-vs-la-clippers-nba-playoffs |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=Deseret News|date=June 16, 2021}}</ref> Conley returned to the lineup in game 6, logging five points and three assists in a 131–119 loss that eliminated the Jazz from the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=MANN SCORES CAREER-HIGH 39, CLIPPERS ELIMINATE JAZZ 131-119 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000226 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

====2021–2023: first-round exit and roster retool====
On August 6, 2021, Conley re-signed with the Jazz on a reported three-year, $72.5 million contract.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mike Conley re-signing with Utah Jazz on 3-year deal |date=August 2, 2021 |url=https://www.deseret.com/2021/8/2/22605907/report-mike-conley-resigning-with-utah-jazz-on-3-year-deal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Mike Conley agrees to stay with Jazz |url=https://www.nba.com/news/report-mike-conley-agrees-to-stay-with-jazz |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> On November 2, he scored a season-high 30 points in a 119–113 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=MITCHELL, CONLEY POWER JAZZ PAST SACRAMENTO 119-113 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100105 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> The Jazz were eliminated in the first round of the playoffs by the Dallas Mavericks, with Conley averaging only 9.2 points and 4.8 assists per game during the 2–4 series defeat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=LUKA DONCIC, MAVERICKS BEAT JAZZ TO ADVANCE TO SECOND ROUND |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100176 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

After the 2021–22 season, the Jazz retooled, trading away their franchise players, All-Stars [[Donovan Mitchell]] and [[Rudy Gobert]]. Conley said he expected to be moved: "I was just like everybody else. I was waiting to get the phone call that I was going somewhere else."<ref>{{Cite web |title=Q&A: Mike Conley explains why he's pleasantly surprised with Utah's strong start |url=https://www.nba.com/news/mike-conley-relishing-jazz-strong-start |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> But he stayed in Utah to start off the 2022–23 season. Conley made his season debut on October 19, recording 13 points, eight assists and two steals in a 123–102 win over the Nuggets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NEW-LOOK JAZZ BEAT NUGGETS 123-102 IN SEASON OPENER |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022200012 |access-date=January 29, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref> Before being traded to Minnesota he averaged nearly 11 points per game.

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2023–2026)===
On February 9, 2023, Conley was traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], with the Jazz acquiring [[Russell Westbrook]], [[Juan Toscano-Anderson]], and [[Damian Jones (basketball)|Damian Jones]], the Lakers acquiring [[Jarred Vanderbilt]], [[Malik Beasley]], and [[D'Angelo Russell]], and the Timberwolves acquiring Conley and [[Nickeil Alexander-Walker]]; the trade reunited Conley with his former Grizzlies teammate [[Kyle Anderson (basketball)|Kyle Anderson]] and Jazz teammate [[Rudy Gobert]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Guards Mike Conley and Nickeil Alexander-Walker from Utah Jazz|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-guards-mike-conley-and-nickeil-alexander-walker-from-utah-jazz|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}}</ref> He made his Timberwolves debut a day later, recording nine points, three assists and two steals in a 128–107 loss to the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Morant has near triple-double as Grizzlies top Timberwolves|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468996|website=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2023}}</ref> On February 23, 2024, he signed a contract extension through the 2025–26 season<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Mike Conley to Contract Extension|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-mike-conley-to-contract-extension|website=NBA.com|date=February 23, 2024|access-date=February 24, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |author-link=Adrian Wojnarowski |date=February 19, 2024 |title=Veteran Conley, T'Wolves agree on extension |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39558626/veteran-leader-conley-rwolves-agree-2-year-extension |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and on May 1, he was again named [[Twyman–Stokes Teammate of the Year Award|NBA Teammate of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Stanton|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Guard Mike Conley Named 2023-24 NBA Twyman-Stokes Teammate of the Year|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-guard-mike-conley-named-2023-24-nba-twyman-stokes-teammate-of-the-year|website=NBA.com|date=May 1, 2024|access-date=May 1, 2024}}</ref>

On February 3, 2026, Conley was traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] as part of a three team trade that also included the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=CHICAGO BULLS ACQUIRE JADEN IVEY AND MIKE CONLEY JR. IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/chicago-bulls-acquire-jaden-ivey-and-mike-conley-jr-in-three-team-trade|website=NBA.com|date=February 3, 2026|access-date=February 4, 2026}}</ref> The next day, Conley and [[Coby White]] were traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in exchange for [[Ousmane Dieng]], [[Collin Sexton]] and multiple second-round draft picks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hornets Acquire Coby White And Mike Conley From Bulls {{!}} Charlotte Hornets |url=https://hornets.com/news/hornets-acquire-coby-white-and-mike-conley-from-bulls |access-date=2026-02-05 |website=hornets.com |language=en}}</ref> On February 5, he was waived by the Hornets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hornets Waive Mike Conley|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-mike-conley|access-date=2026-02-05 |website=hornets.com |language=en}}</ref> Upon clearing waivers, Conley officially re-signed with the Timberwolves on February 17.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Sign Mike Conley |url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-signmike-conley|website=timberwolves.com|date=February 17, 2026|access-date=February 17, 2026}}</ref>

=== Boston Celtics (2026–present) ===
On July 7, 2026, Conley signed a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics Sign Mike Conley |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2026/07/celtics-to-sign-mike-conley.html |access-date=July 6, 2026 |website=Hoops Rumors}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics Sign Mike Conley Jr.
 |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/press-release-20260707-celtics-sign-mike-conley-jr |date=July 7, 2026 |access-date=July 7, 2026 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Conley is a [[Christianity|Christian]] and has spoken about his faith, saying, "[[Jesus]] means the world. Jesus means everything."<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies point guard Conley lives for Jesus on, off basketball court|url=http://www.thealabamabaptist.org/print-edition-article-detail.php?id_art=26840&pricat_art=1|work=thealabamabaptist.org|date=March 7, 2013|access-date=April 25, 2014|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140421095812/http://www.thealabamabaptist.org/print-edition-article-detail.php?id_art=26840&pricat_art=1|archive-date=April 21, 2014}}</ref>

Conley's father is [[Mike Conley Sr.]], an [[Olympic Games|Olympic]] gold and silver medalist in the [[triple jump]]. He is also the nephew of former [[American football]] linebacker [[Steve Conley (linebacker)|Steve Conley]].

On July 5, 2014, Conley married Mary Peluso, whom he met at Ohio State.<ref>{{cite web|last=Nasrallah|first=Ramzy|url=http://www.elevenwarriors.com/ohio-state-basketball/2014/07/37225/mike-conley-got-married-yesterday|title=MIKE CONLEY GOT MARRIED YESTERDAY|work=elevenwarriors.com|date=July 6, 2014|access-date=August 26, 2016}}</ref> They have three sons.{{citation needed|date=January 2025}}

On September 18, 2024, while Conley was in Minneapolis for a [[Minnesota Vikings]] home game, his home was targeted by burglars.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Walsh |first1=Paul |title=Burglars break into Medina home of Timberwolves player and swipe jewels |url=https://www.startribune.com/burglars-break-into-sprawling-home-of-timberwolves-player-and-swipe-jewels/601147138 |website=www.startribune.com |access-date=20 September 2024 |language=en |date=18 September 2024}}</ref>

Conley and [[Trey Alexander]] are cousins.<ref>{{cite web |title=Trey Alexander - 2023-24 - Men's Basketball |url=https://gocreighton.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/trey-alexander/7808 |website=Creighton University Athletics |access-date=30 October 2025 |language=en}}</ref>
